cells.tense: What passes between you and the people nearby is going both directions now, and what's growing in front of you gets tended from more than one side.
cells.ask: Take one thing someone offers you today without handing anything back. Let it end there.
cells.core:
Someone hands you something, you hand something back, and the thing in front of you gets cared for out of that motion. When this runs, you don't have to check whether you've put in enough — it's already even. You can feel it working when a trade finishes and neither side owes anything.

When it runs one way it holds for a while, then it thins. What keeps it is small: someone puts something in your hands and you let them, without evening the score right away. That part gets skipped most often. Nothing here asks you to hold it up alone, and it's fine if the person across from you carries more than you do this week.
cells.sheetLine: What passes between you goes both ways, and you let it.
cells.verb: passing back and forth what each side is carrying
cells.place: in the care of something still growing

cells.tense: You are pushing toward a result that hasn't arrived, and what's growing in front of you is being hurried into a shape it hasn't reached.
cells.ask: Leave one thing you'd normally check on alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You've gotten ahead of something still coming in. Caring how it turns out isn't the problem — that part is good, and it's what keeps the thing tended. But the caring is moving faster than the thing itself, and you can feel it in how often you go back to look at it.

Going in early doesn't get you there sooner. It just takes the time out. Nobody said the result has to be settled today. What's growing can carry itself for one day, and so can you. The part to set down is the going back to check, not the person. That's the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: Let it grow one more day before you reach in.

cells.tense: You have stopped putting much in, and you haven't come around to asking anyone for anything either.
cells.ask: Give one quiet part of your own life twenty minutes today, with no one watching.
cells.core:
Not much is going in or out of this. The hands that used to carry things to people are mostly still, and the asking has gone quiet with them. The thing in front of you is getting along without much from you, and that isn't the same as failing it.

Pushing effort straight at the middle of it won't help. Pick the part of your own life you keep to yourself, the one nobody hears about, and give that part twenty minutes today. No audience, no one told. A person tending something of their own has something to bring back when the time comes. Start with the part that is only yours.

cells.tense: You are setting things right between yourself and other people right now without saying that it is you doing it.
cells.ask: Next time you catch yourself straightening something out between people, say quietly that you just did it.
cells.core:
You straighten things out between people around you, and you haven't called that yours. It reads as just being fair, just what anyone would do. It doesn't feel like a thing you do.

But it is you who moves, and that's been filed under something else. The name is the part worth pointing at, not the fairness. Being able to claim what your hands already do is what lets you trust it. If this reading misses you somewhere, you've still heard what you're doing out there. Keeping things even for the people near you takes attention, and you have been paying it.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping things level, and you haven't said so.

attempts.check: I found myself laying summary onto the record: it lists a card, a seat, a stage, an element and a channel, and nothing about a person knowing or refusing. I would write a tense sentence that tells me what this specific time is made of rather than what the center is doing — and the clearest place that strain shows is the words 'known and not said,' which the record never contains. I could also fairly be told that these are conditions rather than anything anyone chose, and that the ask is then an odd thing to hand over; the way through this is to write the condition as something happening now, and keep the ask optional. The snaps and the 'you've felt it' are dropped for that reason — they serve the reader's authority more than the person.

attempts.check: My draft let the record's own vocabulary do the work: 'keeping what is given and what is received level' is a phrase about the card, not a moment in a life, and the cells then leaned on 'the giving' as a thing rather than people handing things back and forth. The record supports a capacity for fair exchange landing in the care of something still growing; it does not support a history, a duration, or a claim that this is how the person always is. A reader could reasonably say the card names a condition, not a choice, and that the ask then asks too much — so each ask is written as something doable in an ordinary day and ends without a promise. The sentence that served me more than the person is the one that told them what they had already felt; it is gone.

attempts.check: Two rounds of this have shown the same flaw underneath every refused line: I keep reaching for the record's abstractions — exchange, fairness, keeping level — because they sound like the card, and then a verb has to be turned into a noun to carry them. The record actually supports only this: a capacity for give-and-take landing in the care of something still growing. It supports no history, no duration, no 'never' or 'always,' and no first person. A reader could say the ask asks too much of a condition nobody chose, so each ask stays small, doable in an ordinary day, and ends without a promise. The line that served me more than the person was the one telling them what they had already felt; it is gone.

attempts.check: The record says this seat is care for what is growing, and the card is give-and-take through the body's own resonance. It does not say the person has stopped giving for a reason, has been this way for a set time, or is never anything. Each cell states what the capacity is doing in ordinary moments and leaves the past where the person has not handed it over. A reader could say a capacity is not a choice, so the ask is written small and finished by the end of a day, and it survives a miss. The line that served the writer was the one telling the person what they had already felt, and it is gone.
